clue.text: Suffering vicious canine attack is tough

definitions.meaning: read literally: savagely nipped by a dog, its teeth sunk in with force
the everyday sense: hardened, stubborn, not easily moved

explanation.surface: Someone mauled by a savage dog is said to be a tough character.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound is an idiom for a person made stern and uncompromising by experience; the first reading takes its two words literally.

clue.text: Vigorous man with creative aspirations

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
arty describes someone with artistic pretensions

explanation.surface: A robust fellow who also nurses artistic ambitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a hale, energetic person or a robust appetite is vigorous.

clue.text: Left wing tabloid certain to arouse fury

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun, a thing that provokes anger

parts.note: red is the colour of socialism and the political left
rag is a dismissive name for a down-market newspaper

explanation.surface: A left-leaning popular newspaper is bound to infuriate its opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from the cloth waved at a bull, said to enrage it; the definition describes such a provocation rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something that reliably provokes anger, from the matador's cape.

clue.text: I forbid parades arranged by a flapper

indicators.note: arranged says these letters are put into a different order to form a new phrase

explanation.surface: Someone bans processions, and a flapper of the 1920s is blamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flapper' suggests a jazz-age young woman; here it means a creature that flaps its wings. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical bird with showy plumage flaps its wings, so it is literally a flapper.

clue.text: Assignment for Anglican working party

parts.note: a task is a piece of work assigned
taken as written
CE stands for Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A job handed to a group from the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a group set up for a special job is a working party.

clue.text: A feeling of languor in France

definitions.text: A feeling of languor in France

parts.words: A feeling of languor in France
parts.note: the word the French use for listless boredom, borrowed unchanged into English

explanation.surface: Lethargy experienced by someone on holiday in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A loanword from French meaning weariness and listless dissatisfaction.

clue.text: A powder most alchemists carried

indicators.note: carried means the letters are held within the words most alchemists

explanation.surface: Alchemists generally bore a dusting powder with them.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft mineral ground into a powder used on skin; a direct example.

clue.text: I'm unable to get beer around Spanish port

indicators.note: around means the beer word is placed round the other piece

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
I can't is another way of saying I'm unable

explanation.surface: Someone complains they can't find a beer anywhere in a Spanish harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish port' could suggest a wine, but Alicante is the Costa Blanca city; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city on Spain's Costa Blanca, an example of the category.

clue.text: Capital may be initially reinvested by artist

parts.note: can and may both express being able or allowed
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of the word reinvested

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: Money might be put back into the business at first by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, but it is a seat of government. 'by' is a link, meaning beside.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is Australia's seat of government, an example of a national capital.

clue.text: Practise self-denial to appease the gods

definitions.meaning: give things up, go without for a greater good
offer up slaughtered animals or goods on an altar to placate deities

explanation.surface: Going without pleasures in order to keep the deities happy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both giving things up personally and making ritual offerings to deities.

clue.text: Summer bonus for a ophiophilist

definitions.meaning: one who sums, someone or something that does addition
an ophiophilist loves snakes, so finding a viper would be a treat

explanation.surface: A seasonal perk for a snake enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' reads as the season but means a person who adds up. The British viper is a venomous snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a calculating person or machine and Britain's only venomous snake.

clue.text: Consciousness of Este nians'ill-treatment

indicators.note: giving the word rough treatment knocks its letters out of order

parts.note: the scanned text garbles the word Estonians, people from Estonia, with one letter misread and a stray space

explanation.surface: Awareness of how people from Estonia have been abused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; the possessive apostrophe adds no letter, and the scanned clue mangles the nationality word.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: feeling or awareness through the senses, as in losing sensation in a limb.

clue.text: Dash away to detach the plastic cover?

definitions.meaning: rip off a wrapper or seal, the question mark marking the playful reading

explanation.surface: Hurrying off to pull the wrapping from a new purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means both hurtle off and rip something off; the strip on packaging is named for that motion.

clue.text: Repeat it in front of English judge

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece before the rest

parts.note: taken as written
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: An instruction to say something again ahead of an English judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to do or say over again.

clue.text: Only teacher telling boys to play up

definitions.text: Only teacher telling boys to play up

parts.words: Only teacher telling boys to play up
parts.note: the one schoolmaster whose job is urging pupils to play hard, with 'play up' sounding like encouraging misbehaviour

explanation.surface: The single member of staff who encourages pupils to misbehave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play up' usually means misbehave, but on the games field it is the old cry 'Play up!' urging the team on.
explanation.definitionFit: The school games teacher is the one who exhorts pupils to play hard on the field.

clue.text: Farmhand displays his new red convertible

indicators.note: convertible says the letters can be changed into another form

explanation.surface: A farm worker shows off his brand-new red open-top car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convertible' suggests a car but signals the rearrangement. 'displays' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm worker who tends pigs, a specific kind of hand.

clue.text: Tease a trainee with droll, suggestive humour

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them
L is the learner plate on a trainee driver's car
dry humour is droll and understated

explanation.surface: Poking fun at a newcomer with witty, risqué jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: coarse, risqué talk or jokes.

clue.text: Ordinary chap, but a neat worker

definitions.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so this is someone who works with cattle

parts.note: stock means standard or commonplace, as in a stock reply
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: An average fellow who is nevertheless a tidy workman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy, but here is the old word for cattle. 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm hand who looks after livestock, especially cattle, which is what neat once meant.

clue.text: Bury me with confidential notebook! demands broker

parts.note: to inter is to bury
taken as written
a diary is a private daily record

explanation.surface: A dealer insists on being buried with a private journal.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between who arranges deals between parties, like a broker.

clue.text: Fight with Egyptian leads to awkward situation

parts.note: a scrap is a brawl or fight
E is an abbreviation for Egyptian, as in the Egyptian pound

explanation.surface: A brawl with someone from Egypt lands people in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a predicament or difficulty, as in getting into a scrape.

clue.text: Insist on a lock up being provided

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Demanding that a padlock be fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' reads as a door fastening but is a lock of hair; 'up' turns TRESS into SSERT. 'being provided' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare or maintain something forcefully, as in asserting one's rights.

clue.text: Rural paradise makes scoundrel burst into song

indicators.note: burst into means the rogue breaks inside the song

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: Countryside bliss leads a rogue to break into song.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after a Greek region pictured as an idyllic pastoral land.

clue.text: Knight entered enclosure in the amphitheatre

indicators.note: entered means the knight goes inside the enclosure word

parts.note: an area can be an enclosed space
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight on horseback rode into the ring of a Roman amphitheatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The central floor of an amphitheatre where contests took place, by extension the whole building.

clue.text: The consequences of owning property

definitions.meaning: results or outcomes of an action
personal belongings, as in personal goods left in a will

explanation.surface: The results that come from having possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means both results and personal belongings.

clue.text: Mother has a picture inlaid with precious metals

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, such as a horse
a scene is a view or picture

explanation.surface: A mother owns a painting decorated with gold and silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes metalwork decorated in the style of Damascus, with gold or silver worked into steel.

clue.text: Passing fad to produce crackled porcelain

definitions.meaning: to cover a glaze with a network of fine cracks

explanation.surface: A trend for making porcelain with a cracked finish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a short-lived fashion and the fine cracking of a ceramic glaze.

clue.text: American tug

definitions.meaning: an informal word for someone from the United States

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a US citizen and a verb for a sudden pull.

clue.text: Prior to plummeting container becomes white-hot

indicators.note: prior to places the container word ahead of the falling word

parts.note: a can is a container
plummeting is a steep descent

explanation.surface: Before plunging to earth, a vessel glows white-hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: glowing with intense heat.
